title: School education
subtitle: primary school, terms, break the rules
summary: Talk about the school system, the school timetable and the rules pupils have to follow.

lesson.heading: State schools and private schools
lesson.text: In most parts of England and Wales, **state schools** are free and operated by the country. Parents pay to send their children to **private schools**. Students at school are called **pupils**.

examples.text: Both my children go to the local **state school**, so we pay nothing.
My parents sent me to a **private school**.

lesson.heading: The school system, age by age
rows: Almost all children **attend** nursery school for up to 15 hours a week. (attend = go to; formal)
Pupils **take** GCSE exams in up to ten subjects. Then they can go to a college for **vocational training**, e.g. hotel management, or stay at school for two more years.
Pupils take 'A' level exams in three or four subjects. Then they can leave school and **get a job**, **go on to university** or go to a college for **further education**.
lesson.note: Vocational training is training for a particular job.

lesson.heading: The school timetable
lesson.text: The school day is **divided into** about five to seven **lessons**, and over a week most pupils **do** or **study** about ten **subjects**, including English, maths, history and science. There is usually a one-hour lunch **break**, and a break in the morning and afternoon too.

examples.text: The school **timetable** is more or less the same every day.
The day is **divided into** seven lessons.
There is a **break** three times a day.
examples.note: a break = a period of rest between work

lesson.heading: The school year
lesson.text: The school year is usually divided into three **terms** of about 13 weeks. At the end of the year, pupils take exams before they **break up**; after the summer holidays they **go back** for the new school year.

examples.text: There were three **terms** in the school year.
examples.note: a term = a period of study

examples.text: Schools often **break up** after they finish exams.
We **go back** in September for the new school year.

lesson.heading: School rules
lesson.text: **Rules** tell you what you must or must not do. If you **break the rules**, you are **punished**: you may have to **stay behind** after the other pupils leave. If you do something wrong and are punished, you **get into trouble**.

examples.text: If you **broke the rules**, you were **punished**.
Pupils sometimes had to **stay behind** and write an essay.
I used to **get into trouble** for wearing lipstick.
The teachers are not as **strict** now.
examples.note: a strict teacher punishes pupils who do something wrong

lesson.heading: Uniform and atmosphere
lesson.text: We had to call the **male** teachers 'sir' and the **female** teachers 'miss', and we had to **wear** a horrible **uniform**. Nowadays the **atmosphere** is more **relaxed**: older pupils can often **dress** the way they want, as long as they are reasonably **smart**.

examples.note: a uniform = special clothes for a school or a job

examples.text: My school had a really nice, **relaxed atmosphere**.
examples.note: atmosphere = the feeling in a place

examples.text: Pupils can **dress** the way they want.

examples.note: = well dressed and not too casual

lesson.text: In British English the subject is **maths**; in American English it is *math*.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with the words that follow it.
At the age of five, children in England go to ___ school.
exercises.explanation: Children start primary school at five and stay there until they are eleven.

exercises.prompt: At the age of eleven, pupils go to ___ school.
exercises.explanation: Secondary school comes after primary school.

exercises.prompt: When they are sixteen, pupils ___ GCSE exams in up to ten subjects.
exercises.explanation: You take or do an exam - never make an exam.

exercises.prompt: The school ___ is more or less the same every day.
exercises.explanation: The timetable says which lessons you have and when.

exercises.prompt: After their GCSEs, some pupils go to a college for ___ training, e.g. travel and tourism.
exercises.explanation: Vocational training prepares you for a particular job.

exercises.prompt: Nowadays a lot of pupils ___ to university after they leave school.
exercises.explanation: Go on to university = continue your education at university.

exercises.prompt: The school day is divided ___ seven lessons.
exercises.explanation: Something is divided into parts, not divided out of them.

exercises.prompt: Schools often break ___ after the pupils finish their exams.
exercises.explanation: Break up = end classes for the term.

exercises.prompt: There were three ___ in the school year, each about 13 weeks long.
exercises.explanation: A term is one period of study in the school year.

exercises.prompt: I occasionally got into ___ at school for doing things I shouldn't do.
exercises.explanation: Get into trouble = do something wrong and be punished.

exercises.prompt: Is the word about the school system or about school rules?
Say what teachers do when pupils do something wrong.
exercises.answer: The teachers punished pupils who broke the rules.
exercises.explanation: You break a rule, and then you are punished.

exercises.statement: In England pupils take their 'A' level exams when they are sixteen.
exercises.explanation: In England pupils take their 'A' level exams when they are eighteen. GCSE exams are at sixteen.
